components.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sensor
info: Power VCC from 5 V and connect GND to the controller ground.
ECHO can output a 5 V signal. Use a level shifter or voltage divider with 3.3 V-only controller inputs.
Send a short trigger pulse to Trig, then measure how long Echo stays high to calculate distance.

components.name: PCA9685 16-Channel Servo Driver
info: V+ powers the servo rail. Use an external supply matched to your servos (commonly 5–6 V); 6 V is not right for every servo.
VCC powers the driver logic. Keep it at the controller logic voltage (typically 3.3 V or 5 V). Do not confuse VCC with V+.
Connect the external supply ground to PCA9685 GND and the controller ground so all grounds are common.
The PCA9685 communicates with the controller over I²C.

components.name: ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1
info: Power the board through one supported input at a time: USB, 5 V, or regulated 3.3 V, with GND.
GPIO signals use 3.3 V logic; do not drive GPIO pins with 5 V signals.
GPIO43 is UART0 TX and GPIO44 is UART0 RX.
GPIO19 and GPIO20 are also used for native USB D- and D+.
GPIO48 drives the onboard addressable RGB LED.
GPIO0 is the BOOT pin and EN is reset; check boot-strapping requirements before using them as general I/O.

components.name: ESP32-S3 Super Mini
info: Use the 5V input or USB-C for board power; 3V3 is the regulated output. Connect GND to the shared circuit ground.
GPIO pins use 3.3 V logic. Do not connect 5 V signals directly to a GPIO.
The front 2×9 header pin order varies by clone; this definition uses 5V, GND, 3V3, IO1–IO6 on the left and TX, RX, IO13–IO7 on the right, USB end up.
Some versions expose additional GPIO pads on the underside; this drawing models the front 18-pin header only.

components.name: N20 Micro Metal Gearmotor 100 RPM (6 V)
info: Pololu item 2218 reference: 6 V, 298:1 gear ratio, about 100 RPM no-load speed.
No-load current is about 100 mA; extrapolated stall current is 1.6 A. Avoid stalling the motor, and size the driver for startup/stall current.
Use an H-bridge motor driver and a separate motor supply. Do not drive the motor directly from a microcontroller GPIO; share ground with the controller.
10 × 12 mm gearbox cross-section, 3 mm D-shaped output shaft, and extended rear shaft for optional encoder use.

components.name: IR Obstacle Avoidance Sensor
info: Power VCC from 3.3–5 V and connect GND to the controller ground.
OUT is a digital active-low signal: it goes LOW when reflected IR indicates an obstacle.
Use the blue potentiometer to adjust sensitivity/detection range; actual range varies with the module and target surface.
If powering the module from 5 V, verify OUT voltage is safe for a 3.3 V controller input.

components.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display (Blue)
info: 0.96 inch, 128 × 64 blue OLED module with SSD1306-compatible I²C interface.
This reference module uses VCC, GND, SCL, SDA in that order; some visually similar boards reverse VCC/GND or use a different order, so check the silkscreen on your board.
The referenced module accepts 3.3–5 V power. I²C address is commonly 0x3C, but clones may differ.

components.name: Motor Driver - Dual TB6612FNG (1A)
info: SparkFun ROB-14451 style breakout with separate logic supply (VCC) and motor supply (VM).
Logic supply is 2.7–5.5 V; motor supply is up to 15 V. Pull STBY high to enable the driver.
Rated about 1.2 A average per channel and 3.2 A peak. Peak is brief; check motor stall current and driver cooling.
Connect controller ground, driver ground, and motor-supply ground together. Do not connect AO1/AO2/BO1/BO2 directly to GPIO.
The breakout combines a 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope; communicate over I²C.
VCC is typically 3.3–5 V on GY-521 boards, but the MPU-6050 signal pins use 3.3 V logic. Check your board revision before using 5 V logic.
I²C address defaults to 0x68; set AD0 high to use 0x69. INT is an optional interrupt output.
components.name: GY-521 MPU-6050 6-DOF IMU

info: Classic 5 V, 16 MHz Nano with ATmega328P; board revisions and clones may use different USB connectors or chips.
Use a regulated 5 V supply on the 5V pin, or a suitable higher input through VIN. One 3.7 V cell is too low for VIN.
Digital pins D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, and D11 support PWM. A4/A5 are the usual I²C SDA/SCL pins.
components.name: Arduino Nano (ATmega328P)

info: Default value is 220 Ω (red-red-brown-gold bands). Double-click a placed resistor to enter another value; its bands update automatically.
Use the resistor as a passive two-terminal part. The color bands show the nearest standard four-band code for the entered resistance.
components.name: Resistor (editable value)

info: 3.6–3.7 V is nominal; a typical cell reaches 4.2 V when fully charged. Exact capacity and safe discharge current depend on the cell model.
Use a proper Li-ion charger and protection. A single cell cannot directly power a 4.8–6 V SG90 servo or the Nano VIN pin; use an appropriate regulator and share ground.
components.name: 18650 Li-ion Cell (3.7 V)

info: Typical SG90 operating range is 4.8–6 V; use a regulated supply capable of handling startup and stall current.
Brown is GND, red is power, and orange/yellow is the control signal. Wire colors can vary by clone.
Do not power a loaded servo from a Nano GPIO pin. Share ground between the servo supply and controller.
components.name: SG90 9 g Micro Servo
TP4056 USB-C Li-ion Charger (1S)
info: USB-C input is 5 V. This protected module is for one 3.7 V nominal Li-ion/LiPo cell and charges it to 4.2 V; charge current is typically up to 1 A and depends on the board.
Connect the cell to B+ and B−. Connect a load to OUT+ and OUT−; these provide protected battery voltage, not regulated 5 V.
Observe battery polarity and use only a single-cell pack. Board layouts and pad order can vary between TP4056 module versions.

components.name: SPST Slide Switch (On/Off)
info: Generic two-terminal SPST slide switch. Slide the actuator to open or close the connection in a real circuit; this drawing app does not simulate switch state.
Use it in series with the load or signal you want to interrupt. Check the voltage and current rating of the physical switch.

components.name: DRV8833 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver Module
info: Motor supply range is 2.7–10.8 V. The VCC pad shown on this module is the motor supply input (often labeled VM on other boards).
Use IN1–IN4 to control two brushed DC motors, or one bipolar stepper. OUT1/OUT2 are one bridge and OUT3/OUT4 are the other.
Hold SLEEP high to enable the driver. FAULT is an active-low fault output; check whether your specific module adds a pull-up.
The IC can reach 2 A peak per H-bridge; continuous current depends on package, board cooling, supply, and motor conditions. Connect controller and motor-supply grounds together.

components.name: LDR Sensor (Photoresistor, GL5528)
info: Drawn to GL5528 proportions: 5 mm body, 3 mm lead spacing.
Light-dependent resistor: resistance falls as light increases (about 10-20 kOhm at 10 lux, about 1 MOhm in darkness).
Not polarized - either lead can go to either side. Rated about 150 V max and 100 mW.
To read light with a microcontroller, build a voltage divider with a fixed resistor (about 10 kOhm) and connect the midpoint to an analog input.

components.name: Passive Piezo Buzzer (12 mm)
info: Drawn to common 12 mm buzzer proportions with 7.6 mm pin spacing (some parts use 6.5-6.6 mm).
Passive: no built-in oscillator, so it needs a PWM/square-wave tone (for example tone() on Arduino). Steady DC only gives a click.
The housing is marked + and the longer lead is +. Pitch follows the drive frequency; loudest near resonance, typically about 2-4 kHz.
Drive from a GPIO pin (via a small series resistor) or through a transistor for more volume, with the other lead to ground.

components.name: TTP223 Capacitive Touch Module
info: Drawn to the common 15 x 11 mm module size with a 2.54 mm 3-pin header; the ring is the touch pad.
Supply is 2.0-5.5 V. Share ground with the controller; add 100 nF across VCC and GND if you see false triggers.
Default: I/O goes HIGH while touched (momentary, active-high). Solder pads A and B change the output level and toggle mode.
Which pad does which differs between sellers, so check your board's silkscreen. The unlabeled third pad takes a small capacitor to lower sensitivity.
Header order on this drawing is VCC, I/O, GND; some boards print a different order, so confirm on yours.

components.name: Capacitor (Electrolytic, Radial)
info: Drawn to 6.3 x 11 mm radial proportions with 2.5 mm lead spacing (typical of 100 uF 16 V).
Polarized: the longer lead is +; the light stripe with minus marks is the negative side.
Connecting it reversed or above its voltage rating can damage or vent it. Pick a rating well above the supply (about 1.5-2x).
Common uses: power-rail smoothing and decoupling near motors, servos and microcontrollers.

components.name: 5mm Red LED
info: Standard 5mm diffused red light emitting diode.
Longer lead / '+' mark is Anode. Flat rim edge / '-' mark is Cathode. Always use with a current limiting resistor (e.g. 220 Ω to 1 kΩ).

components.name: Tactile Push Button
info: Standard 4-pin momentary tactile button switch.
Pins 1A and 1B are internally connected. Pins 2A and 2B are internally connected. Pressing connects terminal 1 to terminal 2.

components.name: 10k Rotary Potentiometer
info: 10 kΩ linear rotary potentiometer.
Connect pin 1 to VCC, pin 3 to GND, and read variable analog voltage from wiper pin 2.

components.name: 9V Battery (6F22)
info: Standard 9 V rectangular battery (PP3 / 6F22).
Snap terminals on top: circular male stud is positive (+ 9V), octagonal/hex female socket is negative (GND).

components.name: DHT11 Temp & Humidity Sensor
info: Digital temperature and relative humidity sensor breakout module.
Operating voltage 3.3 V to 5 V. Single-wire digital data output pin.

components.name: 5V 1-Channel Relay Module
info: Single-channel 5 V relay module with optocoupler isolation.
Input pins: VCC (5 V), GND, IN (active LOW/HIGH trigger).
Output terminals: NO (Normally Open), COM (Common), NC (Normally Closed) rated for up to 250 VAC / 10 A.

components.name: 1N4007 Rectifier Diode
info: 1 A, 1000 V general-purpose silicon rectifier diode (DO-41).
Cathode terminal is marked with the silver band. Essential for flyback protection across inductive loads like coils and motors.

components.name: Arduino Uno R3
info: Arduino Uno R3 development board featuring the ATmega328P microcontroller.
Operating voltage: 5 V. Recommended input voltage (VIN / Barrel jack): 7-12 V.
14 Digital I/O pins (6 PWM outputs), 6 Analog inputs, 16 MHz clock frequency.

components.name: HC-SR501 PIR Motion Sensor
info: Passive infrared (PIR) motion detector module.
Supply voltage: 4.5 V to 12 V (VCC pin). Digital output signal: 3.3 V HIGH on motion detection, 0 V LOW on idle.
Adjustable sensitivity and delay duration via dual on-board potentiometers.
